data.title: bn-26pp: per-segment registry delta (.reg) sidecar — cold open 38.5x at 250k streams
data.description: Emit each sealed segment's $registry records into a sibling .reg at seal; recovery folds them sequentially instead of one random pread per registration. The log stays the sole registry authority (bn-2di/D1): missing/corrupt/stale/foreign .reg is dropped and the pread path runs, so pre-existing and mixed stores are unaffected. Delta is read once during recovery and never retained (no steady-state RSS). Measured ABBA vs trunk on one corpus: 8GiB/250k cold 9519.7->247.0ms (38.5x), warm 482.8->198.7ms (2.43x); 8GiB/1k cold 65.1->26.7ms, warm 10.2->9.0ms; post-open RSS 173.5->153.9MB; seal drain unchanged within noise. All 14 mess-bench floors pass; 1044 workspace tests pass. Review focus: the accepts_registry_delta cross-check (is the pointer-sidecar layout equality sufficient to make a wrong .reg impossible to fold?), the .reg parser's bounds handling, and whether the SealPack path (seal_pack=on, off by default) silently losing the acceleration is acceptable as a follow-up.
